text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds were quoted largely unchanged in late trade, with the latest German money supply data failing to give any new impulse to the market. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.54, down 0.03 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended flat after an uneventful session which saw them meander in a range of 11/32, dealers said. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-14/32, unchanged from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures failed to hang on to their early gains after a cut in call money and drifted lower in a lacklustre session to test Friday's lows. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.30, down 0.18 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures edged higher ahead of preliminary October consumer price data from three cities which were expected to show a fall in average inflation and open the way for a cut in interest rates later this year. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.50 up 0.76 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities prices opened higher in line with overseas gains. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-11/32, up 2/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.78 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond futures contract ended the Tokyo session with hefty gains after setting an all-time high for any benchmark of 123.70, traders said. In after-hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.65, up 0.65 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A number of dollar deals surfaced during the session. British Columbia launched a 200 million stg bond. A KfW unit issued a $200 million six-year bond at 12 basis points over Treasuries. The spread nudged out to 14 b.p. over but traders said as retail investors started to buy the paper, the spread would actually narrow.
